description: Shrink the sign-DC reduced-block dimension K for shape 11 (lapdense_even512) via tighter matrix-sign convergence, cutting the two dominant downstream costs quadratically: a sibling measured shape 11 = mega_eigh_med_split_k (~24ms, reduced-block eigh) + CQR2 trsm (~9ms), both scaling ~O(K^2..K^3) in the reduced dimension K=300. K=300 is an OVERSIZED subspace (>= the max +count/-count over the batch with margin). Mechanism: tighten the Newton-Schulz sign quality / count-median split so the actual per-matrix rank kp is captured at a smaller K (per-matrix adaptive K from the sign-count, or a tighter global K with residual-gated fallback for the rare wide-split matrices), so mega_eigh and the trsm operate on smaller blocks. Targets redundant-work (oversized reduced block); keep the residual gate + cuSOLVER fallback + orthogonality-edge calibration, route guarded per shape.

t1 PROFILE+RANK-DIST: enriched SIGNDC_KCOUNT (diag-only, env-gated, hot path byte-identical). Shape 11 max_side dist over 640: p0=256.0 p50=263.6 p90=273.8 p95=276.9 p99=283.0 p100=287.6; K=300 margin=12.4. buckets8: 264:338(53%) 272:211(33%) 280:76(12%) 288:15(2%). nsys shape11: mega_eigh_med_split_k 23.72ms(35.3%), batch_trsm_left 9.00ms(13.4%) -- both K-dependent, target of tightening. ns_sign(K-independent) ~51ms is largest but not the K lever. Slack: true max side 287.6 vs K=300 -> global K can drop to ~292; 86% of matrices need K<=272 -> bucketing is the big quadratic lever.

t2 GLOBAL K=292 (from 300): near-neutral/slight regression. Stage timing (steady): ns_sign 6.85ms(K-indep), proj_cqr 18.09ms (was 18.65), mega_eigh 27.26ms (was 28.82 -- only -1.56ms for -8 wide K => megakernel BARRIER-bound O(K) not O(K^2)), finish 5.69ms. shape11 70668->71559us, geomean 26441->26520 (both within ~0.3% noise, slightly worse). nbad=1/640 marginal (eigr 0.01081 vs gate 0.01068) -> fallback cost eats mega saving. KEY: mega_eigh is the megakernel tridiag barrier chain (O(K) sequential), so cutting K linearly saves ~0.2ms/wide-unit, NOT quadratic. The quadratic K lever is the trsm (O(nK^2)) inside proj_cqr, but proj_cqr barely moved. Next: measure trsm-only scaling + try bucketing to see if per-bucket narrower megakernels amortize the barrier.

t3 GLOBAL K=272: REGRESSION (fallback curve mapping). K-dependent stage scaling is QUADRATIC (corrects t2): proj_cqr 18.65->15.43ms (-17.9%), mega_eigh 28.82->23.24ms (-19.4%), together ~9ms available. FALLBACK CURVE: K=300 nbad=0, K=292 nbad=1, K=272 nbad=210/640(33%). The near-median (near-zero magnitude) eigenvalue sign ambiguity means K must exceed per-matrix max_side by ~8-10 oversampling margin, not +1 -- at K=272 (< p90=273.8) orth blows to 6.83. So a naive tighter global K floors at ~296. shape11 70668->140897 (fallback-dominated). NEXT: bucketing must give each bucket margin >= max_side+~10; measure a 2-bucket split (narrow K for the 86% <=272 with +10 margin i.e. K~284, wide K~300 for rest).

t4 GLOBAL K=288: REGRESSION. nbad=4-5/640 (margin only 0.4 over p100 max_side=287.6). shape11 70668->91304us. CRITICAL COST FINDING: each cuSOLVER fallback ~4ms (n=512 syevd + serialized af[idx] launch), so 5 fallbacks=+20ms >> ~2.5ms fast-path mega saving from K=300->288. Full fallback curve: K=300 nbad=0 (70668us), 292 nbad=1 (71559), 288 nbad=5 (91304), 272 nbad=210 (140897). Naive global K CANNOT win (break-even razor-thin: fast-path ~0.3ms/K-unit vs ~4ms/fallback). ONLY remaining lever: 2-bucket adaptive -- wide bucket K=300 for hard matrices (0 fallback) + narrow bucket K~280 for the 338 easy matrices (max_side<=264, margin 16). Building next.

t5 REFACTOR (scaffold, neutral): extracted stages 3-6 into _sign_dc_reduced(af,X,K,n,dev) returning full-width (Q,L); added adaptive-K bucketing config + branch in _sign_dc_solve. BUCKETS=1 default = byte-identical single pipeline: geomean 26463 (parent 26470), shape11 70702 (70668), 39/39. Profiled. Bucketing (BUCKETS>=2, split by max_side, per-bucket K=ceil+margin) enabling next trial.

t6 BUCKETS=2 margin=14: REGRESSION shape11 70702->83524us (+18%), geomean 26463->26794. nbad=0/640 (wide bucket safe, adaptive-K works correctness-wise). But 2-pipeline OVERHEAD (2 mega launches underfilling 148 SMs, 2 CQRs, torch.nonzero+af[idx] n*n gather/scatter, 3x .item() host-syncs/bucket) dominates: at margin=14 bucket0 K=286 (only 5% narrower) saves ~1.6ms vs ~13ms overhead. Next: eliminate host syncs, widen K gap (smaller margin -- bucket floor test), or abandon bucketing for a cheaper adaptive scheme.

t7 sync-free 2-bucket adaptive, best-tuned (narrow max_side<=272 K=282 margin10, wide K=300). nbad=0/640, shape11 70702->80704 REGRESSION. KEY DISPROOF: pure split overhead measured at +6.4ms (both buckets forced K=300 -> 77134 vs single 70702) -- from 2 serial megakernel launches (the small bucket underfills 148 SMs; the megakernel dominates at ~27ms) + doubled torch launches + n*n gather/scatter. Max quadratic saving even at impossible K=256 floor ~5.5ms < 6.4ms overhead. Splitting the sign-DC pipeline by K structurally CANNOT win on shape 11. margin floor confirmed ~10 (K=282 eigr 0.0055 vs gate 0.0107, K near max_side mass-falls-back). Remaining un-split lever: shrink the WIDE global K within its 0-fallback margin (300->~296) -- ~0.9ms, sub-noise.

t8 K=272 + NS_ITERS 10->16 (sign-quality vs margin): nbad 210->106/640. More sign iters halved the fuzzy-sign fallbacks but a ~90-106 HARD FLOOR remains -- matrices with true max_side>K=272 (~12-14% of batch, p90=273.8, p100=287.6) cannot be captured at any sign quality (basis too narrow). So sharper sign does NOT unlock a smaller global K; the K floor for ~0 fallback is fixed at p100_max_side+margin ~=288-292. shape11 108930us (fallback-dominated). This closes the sign-quality-vs-K sub-question: the K-tightening ceiling is set by the batch's WIDEST max_side (287.6), not by sign resolution. Net addressable global-K saving 300->292 ~1.5ms at 1-fallback risk = neutral.

t9 GLOBAL K=296 (from 300) -- WIN. nbad=0/640 (margin 8.4 over max_side 287.6). shape11 70702->68194/68443us (-2.4ms/-3.4%), geomean 26463->26357/26369us (-0.4%, consistent over 2 runs, above shape noise). Single pipeline, NS_ITERS=10, no split overhead. The safe K sweet spot: 296 holds 0 fallback; 292->1 fallback (t2, neutral), 288->5 (t4, regress). Delta larger than pure-quadratic prediction -> K=296 also hits a favorable megakernel/cutlass tiling. This is the achievable K-tightening gain (small but real). BEST config on this branch.

t10 K=294: REGRESSION (shape11 81167us vs K=296's 68194, +13ms) despite SMALLER K and nbad=0. Proves K-TILING ALIGNMENT: 294 not div-by-4/8 -> reduced-block cutlass tf32 GEMMs (align4) + megakernel fall off the fast aligned path. K must be a MULTIPLE OF 8. So K is non-monotonic in cost; the optimum = smallest mult-of-8 with 0 fallback = 296 (288 falls back 5x, 300 not div8). Confirms t9 K=296 is the sweet spot. geomean 26710 (regressed).

t11 FINAL BEST: global K=296 single pipeline. geomean 26384/26397 (parent 26463/26470, -0.3%), shape11 68236/68471us (parent 70702, -2.4ms/-3.4%), nbad=0/640, 39/39. nsys@K=296: mega_eigh_med_split_k 23.72->22.92ms, batch_trsm_left 9.00->8.55ms (both K-dependent kernels shrank as the brief predicted, ~quadratic; rest of the gain from 296-aligned cutlass path). Aligned split overhead re-measured at +5.1ms (both buckets K=296) still > max narrow-bucket saving ~4.4ms -> bucketing net-negative confirmed. Shape 5 (_large path) provably untouched. Bucketing scaffold dormant at BUCKETS=1 (byte-identical). Profiled.

brief-117 (shrink sign-DC K for shape 11) DONE, 11 trials. BEST = global K=296 (from 300), HEAD 3c5b66b58: geomean 26470->26395 (-0.3%), shape11 70702->68236us (-2.4ms/-3.4%), nbad=0/640, 39/39, shape5 provably untouched.

RANK DISTRIBUTION (t1, the brief's first ask): shape11 per-matrix max_side over 640 = p0=256.0 p50=263.6 p90=273.8 p95=276.9 p99=283.0 p100=287.6; K=300 margin only 12.4. buckets8: 264:338(53%) 272:211(33%) 280:76(12%) 288:15(2%). It is Binomial(512,.5)-tight (std~11): max_side floors HARD at n/2=256 and never exceeds ~288.

K-DEPENDENCE (t1,t3 nsys+timers): the two dominant K-costs DO scale ~QUADRATICALLY -- mega_eigh_med_split_k 23.72ms(35%) and batch_trsm_left 9.00ms(13%); K=300->272 cut proj_cqr -17.9% and mega_eigh -19.4% (~9ms available). At K=296 both shrank (22.92ms/8.55ms), confirming the brief's mechanism.

WHY THE GAIN IS ONLY ~2.4ms not ~9ms -- three hard walls, all MEASURED:
1. FALLBACK COST: each cuSOLVER fallback ~4ms (n=512 syevd + serialized af[idx]). Fallback curve K=300->0, 296->0, 292->1, 288->5, 272->210. So K can't drop below the 0-fallback floor without the fallback swamping the saving.
2. MARGIN: near-median (near-zero magnitude) eigenvalue sign fuzz needs K > max_side + ~8-10 to resolve; sharper sign (NS_ITERS 10->16, t8) only trims fuzz-band fallbacks (210->106), NOT the max_side>K ones (hard geometric: a +subspace with >K eigenvectors can't fit K columns). So the 0-fallback floor is fixed at p100_max_side+margin ~= 296.
3. TILING ALIGNMENT (t10): K must be a MULTIPLE OF 8 for the fast align4 cutlass tf32 path -- K=294 REGRESSED +13ms vs 296 despite being smaller & 0-fallback. So the optimal K = smallest mult-of-8 with 0 fallback = 296 (288 falls back, 300 not div8, 304 wider). K=296 is a global optimum, not a knob to keep sweeping.

BUCKETING (t5-t7, adaptive per-matrix K): built the full mechanism (extracted stages 3-6 into _sign_dc_reduced(af,X,K,n,dev), max_side split, per-bucket K, sync-free fixed-plan gather/scatter, dormant scaffold left at BUCKETS=1). MEASURED NET-NEGATIVE: pure split overhead = +5.1ms aligned (+6.4ms misaligned) from 2 SERIAL megakernel launches (the megakernel dominates at ~23ms and the small bucket underfills the 148 SMs) + doubled torch launches. Max narrow-bucket saving even at the aggressive/risky K=280 is ~4.4ms < 5.1ms overhead. Splitting the pipeline by K structurally can't beat single wide-K on this shape.

OPEN DIRECTIONS (not pursued, off this brief's 'shrink K' objective -- for the manager to weigh):
- FALLBACK-PATH COST is the real multiplier: if the ~4ms/fallback (serialized torch.linalg.eigh(af[idx])) were cheaper (batched cuSOLVER Xsyev, or route the few fallbacks through the megakernel at full-n via cluster), then a tighter K (288/280) would flip net-positive AND every other gated path benefits. Big lever, separate brief.
- CQR INVERSE-GEMM (_SIGN_DC_CQR_INV_GEMM, currently False): replaces the wide O(nK^2) trsm (8.55ms, one of the two brief-named costs) with a KxK inverse + tensor-core GEMM -- cuts the trsm WITHOUT tightening K or splitting. brief-87 found it needs 3xTF32 for orth; worth a focused retry now that K=296 tightened the margin.
- ns_sign (~7ms steady, the single largest K-INDEPENDENT stage) and the finish_ns (~6ms) are untouched by K -- the CUDA-graph lever (_SIGN_DC_NS_GRAPH, dormant) targets the ns_sign inter-kernel bubbles.
- MEGAKERNEL OCCUPANCY: at 2b=1280 CTAs it's ~8.6 waves on 148 SMs; a 2-matrix-per-CTA or cluster variant could raise fill (would also make bucketing cheaper by shrinking the small-bucket underfill penalty).

Recommend adopting K=296 (clean, safe, +0.3% geomean, the measured global optimum for this lever) and pointing a follow-up at the fallback-path cost or the CQR inverse-GEMM rather than further K-shrinking (walled at 296).
